items.basis: The proposed radiative cooling coating addresses heat gain from solar radiation but does nothing to address the fundamental failure mode of salt accumulation in the wick channel, which directly causes cooling system failure according to the problem statement.

The candidate fails to address the boundary condition of high humidity environments where evaporative cooling becomes ineffective, yet claims to maintain temperatures below 8°C in these exact conditions without explaining how radiative cooling overcomes this fundamental limitation.

The cited evidence includes a study on radiative cooling for chemical storage tanks, which has different thermal mass and cooling requirements than vaccine storage, and irrelevant studies on dairy research and influenza vaccines that provide no support for the cooling mechanism.

The candidate offers no evidence that the proposed solution performs better than the baseline evaporative cooler, especially in the critical failure scenario of high humidity where evaporative cooling naturally underperforms.

The candidate provides no details on how the radiative cooling coating would be applied to an existing evaporative cooler in last-mile clinics with limited infrastructure, or how it would withstand physical damage and environmental degradation in remote settings.

The candidate fails to address the critical clinic staff need for knowing remaining cooling margin, providing no mechanism for temperature monitoring or warning systems that would indicate when the interior approaches the 8°C failure threshold.
